question: Explain the main features of a Limited Liability Partnership under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.

points.label: Body corporate and separate legal entity
points.description: An LLP is a body corporate formed and incorporated under the Act, a legal entity separate from its partners; it can own property and sue and be sued in its own name.

points.label: Perpetual succession
points.description: An LLP has perpetual succession; a change in partners does not affect its existence, rights or liabilities.

points.label: Limited liability
points.description: The LLP's obligations are met out of its own property; a partner is not personally liable for them merely by being a partner, so a partner's risk is generally limited to the agreed contribution, and a partner is not personally liable for another partner's wrongful act or omission.
points.basis: Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, liability of the LLP and of its partners

points.label: Partners and designated partners
points.description: An LLP must have at least two partners and at least two designated partners who are individuals, with at least one of them resident in India; designated partners are responsible for compliance under the Act.
points.basis: Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, provisions on partners and designated partners

points.label: LLP agreement and partnership law
points.description: The mutual rights and duties of partners are governed by the LLP agreement (or, failing it, by the Act's default provisions); the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 does not apply to an LLP.
points.basis: Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, LLP agreement and non-application of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932
